pron.explain: The agent garbles the city — "Pune" comes out as "pune.com", like a website. City and proper-noun slots are read from text the TTS has never heard aloud, so they break in ways only a listener catches. Tag = City so the fix lands in the right pronunciation dictionary.

issue.setup: Play from the marked moment. The user answers, but listen to the agent — it never registers what was said and carries on as if the line went quiet. Log the issue the way you would in the tool.
issue.explain: The user spoke, but the ASR never captured it, so the agent moved on without the answer — a User input capture error. It's not a wrong response (there was no input to respond to) and not repetition. Picking the right type matters because input-capture errors route to the speech-to-text team, not the prompt team.

issue.setup: Play from the marked moment. The customer points out something factual about the company. Listen to how the agent answers — is what the agent says true, or is it made up?
issue.explain: The customer correctly says Shein is a Chinese company. Instead of acknowledging that, the agent insists “we’re an Indian company” — a made-up factual claim, with no basis, said only to keep the pitch going. That’s wrong / invented information, not repetition and not an irrelevant reply. Factual errors are the highest-trust-risk failures: the agent sounds confident while being flatly wrong, and only a human who is listening catches it.

issue.setup: Play from the marked moment. This is a first-contact call. Listen to what the agent claims has already happened between them and the customer — and how the customer reacts.
issue.explain: On a first call, the agent claims “last time we arranged a consultant meeting for you” — an event that never happened. The customer’s own reply (“what consultant are you even asking about?”) confirms it was invented. Fabricating a prior relationship is made-up information, not an irrelevant reply. These invented details break trust instantly, and they’re exactly the kind of thing telemetry can’t see but a human hears at once.
